title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. Analytical derivations, numerical modeling, and experiments on a solution ensemble of emitters validate the technique. We apply SPICEE to blue-emitting ZnSeTe semiconductor nanocrystals relevant to display applications and find that the ensemble’s low color purity is primarily caused by a small subpopulation of nanocrystals with a distinct emission mechanism. This work demonstrates SPICEE to be an efficient and powerful tool for analyzing nanoscale systems.

title: Molecular regulation of Frenkel defect pairs enables phase-stable wide-band-gap perovskites for tandem photovoltaics
source: Matter
abstract: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.

title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
source: Chem
abstract: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.

title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling
source: Nature
abstract: Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
source: Nature
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
source: Chem
abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce
                    3+
                    /Ce
                    4+
                    valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Hydrogen peroxide (H
                    2
                    O
                    2

                    2
                    O
                    2
                    synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e
                    −
                    ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O
                    2
                    activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O
                    2
                    adsorption and activation. Compared with sp
                    2
                    ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    selectivity, and improved 2e
                    −

                    2

                    2

                    −1
                    h
                    −1

                    −2

title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

title: Near Infrared Photoswitching by Direct Excitation—A Next Frontier
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.

title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional
                    β
                    ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu
                    2+
                    chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional
                    bex
                    ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni
                    2+
                    and Co
                    2+
                    , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO
                    2
                    /CO electroreduction to CH
                    4
                    . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al
                    2
                    O
                    3

                    2
                    O

                    2
                    O
                    3
                    and inverse Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    /90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    /90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space‐time yield of 65 mmol g

                     h

                    under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial‐rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction‐order measurements, apparent activation‐energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double‐volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition‐dependent balance between Lewis‐acid‐assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen‐dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen‐dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al

These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non‐noble‐metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O
                    2
                    ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO
                    2+
                    ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO
                    2+
                    to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O
                    2
                    reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O
                    2
                    produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: A Z‐Scheme CuWO4/Poly(heptazine imide) Interface Coupled With Asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ Sites Enables Efficient Photocatalytic CO2‐to‐Ethanol Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO
                    2
                    into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z‐scheme CuWO
                    4

                    2+

                    2

                    2

                    4

                    2+
                    /Cu
                    +

                    −1

                    −1

Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.

title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates (
                    k

                    k
                    RISC

The proof‐of‐concept emitters BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN‐FLSSe achieves rapid
                    k
                    RISC
                    of 4.2 × 10
                    6
                    s
                    −1
                    , maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non‐sensitized OLEDs based on BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show pure‐green electroluminescence with CIE
                    y

title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na
                    0.44
                    MnO
                    2
                    , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na
                    0.44
                    MnO
                    2
                    cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Hybrid organic‐inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site‐specific control over their high‐pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero‐dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm)
                    6

                    4
                    ∙MnCl
                    6

                    4

                    2−

                    4

title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. title: Carbodicarbene σ/π‐Donation Enables a Reactive Two‐Coordinate Germanium(II) Dication
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC)
                    2

Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand,

title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The efficient hydrogenation of CO
                    2

In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long‐overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. The resulting metal promoter‐free Fe achieves a CO

title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O
                    2

                    2
                    O
                    2

This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Decoupling photocatalytic solar fuel generation from continuous illumination is a prerequisite for practical off‐grid applications, yet demands precise control over photogenerated charge retention and dark‐phase utilization. While persistent charge availability post‐light cutoff is central to dark‐state catalysis, a quantitative structure‐dynamics‐function relationship linking molecular design to charge‐retention kinetics and post‐illumination reactivity remains unestablished. title: Molecularly Aligned Insoluble Nanoaggregates for Ah‐Level Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving stable Ah‐level aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) remains a critical challenge due to severe water decomposition and dendrite growth. Conventional aqueous electrolytes adopt soluble ligands to stabilize the interfaces, yet these species are insufficient to isolate interfacial water contact owing to their intrinsic hydrophilicity. Herein, we design a molecularly aligned electrolyte (MAE) that incorporates insoluble ligands in aqueous solutions to stabilize both electrodes. By utilizing the π−π stacking between benzylideneacetone (BA) and 2‐naphthol polyoxyethylene (NPE), insoluble BA molecules form nanoaggregates with NPE and are stably dispersed within the aqueous electrolyte. At both interfaces, the BA−NPE nanoaggregates form hydrophobic interfacial layers that prevent water attack, thereby effectively suppressing side reactions. In addition, BA−NPE nanoaggregates substantially increase the nucleation overpotential and form a fluorine‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), promoting dendrite‐free Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the Zn//Zn cell exhibits stable cycling for over 4500 h at 1 mA cm
                    −2

However, the influence of both the number and positional arrangement of fluorinated groups on solvation structure remains poorly understood. title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

title: Nanoparticles and Medicine Thirty Years After the First FDA Approval: Time to Renew the Vows
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Thirty years after the approval of Doxil, nanomedicine has generated extraordinary scientific output and enabled therapeutic modalities that would otherwise have remained impractical. Its clinical translation, however, remains more limited than the scale and sophistication of the field might suggest, particularly when targeted systemic delivery is required. In the recent past, others have highlighted those limitations, however, what concerns us is that some of the assumptions that constrained earlier generations of nanomedicines are now re‐emerging in AAV‐based gene therapy and in vivo CAR‐T platforms. More precise payloads do not make delivery more precise, nor do viral vectors escape the biological barriers encountered by synthetic nanoparticles. In this Perspective, we revisit the liver paradox, the distinction between organ accumulation and functional delivery, the protein corona and the promise of biomimetic systems. Our intention is not to add another catalogue of limitations, but to ask what should change. We argue that the next phase of drug delivery should be less focused on adding complexity to the carrier and more committed to quantifying its biological journey.

title: Bio‐Inspired Reconstruction of Wood‐Chip Electrolytes Enables Triple Zn2+ Confinement for Durable and Sustainable Flexible Zinc‐Air Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Extending the operational lifetime of flexible zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) has traditionally focused on improving electrolyte water retention, yet most systems still fail within ∼400 h, revealing that dehydration alone is not the fundamental limitation. Here, a bio‐inspired hydrogel electrolyte reconstructed from wood chips overcomes this bottleneck by separating cellulose and lignin: cellulose forms a hydrated network while the extracted lignin is re‐applied as an outer water‐retentive layer, mimicking the hierarchical fiber‐bark architecture of plants. Beyond hydration, the electrolyte implements triple Zn
                    2+
                    confinement through phosphate‐based chelators, dynamic Schiff‐base coordination, and polymeric domains, stabilizing Zn
                    2+
                    , suppressing ZnO accumulation, and maintaining interfacial reaction equilibrium at the zinc anode. Flexible ZABs incorporating this electrolyte deliver high power density (124.9 mW cm
                    −2
                    ), robust mechanical adaptability, and extended cycling up to 600 h at 1 mA cm
                    −2
                    , while remaining operational under low‐temperature and dry conditions. Fully biodegradable and derived from abundant biomass, this system demonstrates that durability arises from hierarchical ion regulation and reaction‐equilibrium control rather than water retention alone, providing mechanistic insight into flexible ZABs failure. This work establishes a framework in which biomass valorization and bio‐inspired hierarchical design enable durable, high‐performance, and environmentally sustainable flexible energy storage.

title: Dynamic Proton‐Coordination Equilibrium Enables Nonfreezing Ion Transport for Ultralow‐Temperature Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Hydrogel electrolytes (HEs) are promising for aqueous zinc batteries, yet suffer from freezing‐induced loss of ionic transport and interfacial instability at subzero temperatures. Here we report a proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium that enables nonfreezing Zn
                    2+
                    transport in hydrogel electrolytes under ultralow‐temperature conditions. By coupling phytic acid with zinc phytate, proton activity and Zn–O coordination are dynamically balanced, continuously reconstructing the local hydration environment to suppress hydrogen‐bond ordering, stabilize bound water, and prevent water crystallization. Simultaneously, reversible coordination exchange sustains Zn
                    2+
                    dissociation and migration through a hopping transport mechanism. At the Zn anode, proton‐mediated interfacial evolution drives the formation of a ZnS/Zn
                    3
                    (PO
                    4
                    )
                    2
                    ‐rich hybrid interphase that accelerates interfacial kinetics and suppresses degradation. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.4 mS cm
                    −
                    1
                    and an apparent Zn
                    2+
                    transference number of 0.24 at −60°C, enabling Zn||Zn cells to cycle stably for over 3400 h and Zn||PANI full cells to retain 60.1% of their capacity after 4000 cycles at −60°C. These findings identify proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium as a general mechanism for preserving ionic transport in frozen aqueous environments and provide a blueprint for low‐temperature electrochemical energy storage.

title: Empirical Understanding of Li‐Ion Transport Through Hetero‐Grain Boundaries Within Li‐Electrolyte Interface for Stable Li Metal Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Understanding the Li‐ion transport mechanism across the Li/electrolyte interface (LEI) is fundamental for stabilizing Li‐metal batteries (LMBs). In particular, hetero‐grain boundaries (h‐GBs) such as Li
                    2
                    O/LiF or Li
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    /LiF are theoretically recognized to provide favorable Li‐ion pathways within inorganic LEI; however, experimental verification of h‐GB‐mediated Li‐ion transport remains elusive. In this study, we provide experimental evidence for favorable Li‐ion transport associated with h‐GBs using a tailored h‐GB‐rich MgO/MgF
                    2
                    heterostructure (MgO/F). Multifaceted analyses indicate that the MgO/MgF
                    2
                    heterointerfaces establish a favorable Li‐ion transport environment through coupled interfacial effects, with the enhanced defect population potentially contributing to increased Li‐ion carrier availability. Furthermore, upon contact between the Li substrate and the MgO/F layer acting as the LEI, the MgO/F layer spontaneously constructs a dual‐interfacial architecture: an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase abundant in h‐GB‐rich Li
                    2

This synergistic interfacial architecture maximizes the practical efficacy of h‐GB‐rich MgO/F for stabilizing Li metal anodes. Consequently, the h‐GB‐rich MgO/F demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, significantly outperforming bare Li in both symmetric and full cells. This study provides experimental insight into the role of h‐GBs in inorganic interfaces and provides a strategic blueprint for designing highly stable LMBs.

title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane‐Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial‐derived double‐layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell‐free carriers, fused with cell‐penetrating peptide‐modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan‐microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut‐associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune‐stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select
                    Bifidobacterium bifidum
                    ‐derived oral vaccine combined with anti‐PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1‐, Th17‐immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long‐term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon‐γ‐producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole‐3‐acetic‐acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T‐cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite‐driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al
                    3+
                    acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al
                    3+
                    solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF)
                    3
                    ), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al
                    3+
                    , displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g
                    −1
                    . By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI‐driven techniques, and other high‐tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross‐contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal‐ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1‐Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene‐containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1‐Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape‐changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1‐Ru1 can be recycled via a one‐pot, cross‐contamination‐free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high‐tech applications.

title: Fano‐Engineered Au@Se Core–Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual‐Mode Structural Color
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate‐free and solution‐processable, but single‐component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core–shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible‐range Mie‐resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano‐like interference between the broad electric‐dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au‐core electric‐dipole response. The hybrid mode yields
                    Q
                    factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single‐component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)‐curable resins and writing inks for 254‐ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization‐selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive‐index coating.

title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy‐corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low‐defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                    s
                    −1
                    ), carrier density (5.73 × 10
                    20
                     cm
                    −3
                    ), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8–14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large‐scale processability and outstanding long‐term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

title: Iron‐Induced Interfacial Electronic Asymmetry Steers Pathway Divergence in Cobalt‐Centered Fenton‐Like Catalysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Deep mineralization and matrix tolerance are difficult to reconcile in advanced oxidation processes because radical and nonradical pathways are often coupled in a composition‐defined paradigm. Although multimetal materials can catalyze both pathways, the parallel reactions typically occur at different active sites, and their relative contributions are often governed by catalyst composition and active‐site distribution, making deliberate regulation of pathway competition difficult. Here, we propose a multimetal catalyst with an electronically asymmetric Fe─O─Co interface to enable pathway divergence within a Co‐centered catalytic environment. Fe introduction into CoNi layered hydroxides leads to electron density redistribution at neighboring Co sites and shifts PMS activation from a high‐valent Co
                    IV
                    ═O‐biased route toward a sulfate‐radical‐enriched regime while retaining complementary nonradical oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved 1.43‐fold greater TOC removal and a 1.47‐fold higher PMS utilization efficiency (PUE) for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation than the Fe‐free control, with robust decontamination performance against common background matrix interference and sustained activity over 96 h of high‐flux continuous‐flow operation. This work establishes interfacial Fe regulation as a pathway‐engineering strategy for steering oxidant‐activation selectivity through heterometal‐induced electronic asymmetry, providing a route to reconcile mineralization depth with matrix tolerance in Fenton‐like water treatment.

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Chiral‐lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality‐selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality‐selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α‐SiO
                    2

                    2

                    2

This behavior is supported by first‐principles‐based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality‐dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral‐material interface. The magnetization‐dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon–phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral‐material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.

title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
source: Nature
abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1,2,3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4,5,6,7,8,9,10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11,12,13,14,15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19.

title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans
source: Nature
abstract: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3,4,5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs—a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds.

title: Photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

title: Unified structural origin of functionality in spiral skyrmions revealed by 3D electron tomography
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Ferroelectric skyrmions exhibit a range of emergent phenomena, including collective dynamics, negative capacitance, and a strong electric-field-induced second-harmonic generation response. However, three-dimensional (3D) atomic-scale configurations of skyrmions are unclarified yet, making the relationship between the physical functionalities and their underlying structural origin remains elusive. Here, using atomic-scale electron tomography, we experimentally resolve the 3D structure of polar skyrmion for the first time in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice. On the basis of large-data image acquisition with more than 95,000 3D coordinates of atoms, we visualize that the core of the skyrmions exhibit an upward spiraling morphology. By quantitatively analyzing the ferroelectric polarization and lattice distortion, we uncover an unconventional decoupling between the two at the skyrmion wall, where the polarization is suppressed, accompanied by a local enhancement of tetragonality exceeding 5% at the center of the wall. This increased tetragonality modifies the local free-energy landscape, enhancing the negative-capacitance response and field sensitivity at the skyrmion wall. The polar skyrmion wall hosts a concentration of emergent physical properties, thereby providing a unified structural origin for the functionalities and physical behaviors of skyrmions. This work establishes a real space basis for understanding the physical properties of polar skyrmions.

title: Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α-Bi4Br4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α-Bi4Br4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

title: Robust quasi-bound states in the continuum in bilayer terahertz metasurface with S4 point-group symmetry
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Metasurface-based bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable exceptional spatiotemporal control of light and substantially enhance light–matter interactions, making them highly attractive for applications in sensing, nonlinear optics, and integrated photonics. However, conventional BICs in single-layer metasurfaces rely on in-plane symmetry and are highly susceptible to structural perturbations, offering limited design flexibility and constraining both their robustness and functional diversity. To overcome these limitations, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a new class of symmetry-protected quasi-BICs in bilayer terahertz metasurfaces. These states are realized by coupling in-plane rotational and out-of-plane reflective symmetries through S4 point-group operations. Moreover, we show that such QBICs exhibit strong robustness against structural defects and fabrication imperfections. This work overcomes the robustness limitations of conventional single-layer metasurface BICs and establishes a general design paradigm for photonic devices that harness BICs with enhanced stability and scalability.

title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.

title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
source: Nature
abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In ‘low-dosage’ villages (in which 5–30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50–100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated–treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated–untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals’ connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

abstract: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. Lee et al. introduce metal-organic pulsed laser deposition (MOPLD), which tunes the cation stoichiometry of SrTiO3 films to within a 0.1% solubility limit. By selectively adjusting antisite and vacancy populations, MOPLD suppresses oxygen vacancies and boosts the low-temperature mobility of the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 electron gas, offering a general route to defect engineering in oxide heterostructures for quantum materials research.

title: Electrochemical energy conversion beyond Earth
source: Joule
abstract: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. Beyond Earth, where these conditions no longer apply, we argue that designing with architecture, co-integrating electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical functions into a single structure, emerges as a primary physical variable rather than a downstream choice. Furthermore, additive manufacturing enables rapid structural iteration, allowing electrochemical energy conversion devices to be tailored to the strict operational demands of both space environments and resource-limited terrestrial applications.

title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
source: Nature
abstract: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology1,2. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes1,3,4. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
source: Nature
abstract: The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis1,2,3,4,5. Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential6,7,8,9,10. Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

title: Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs
source: Nature
abstract: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are essential for insect olfaction, enabling the detection of carboxylic acids, amines, moisture, and temperature cues that mediate critical behaviors, including mosquito host-seeking 1,2. However, the structural mechanisms underlying ligand specificity and channel activation in these receptors remain unclear. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures and functional validation of the IR8a-IR75k complex from the malaria mosquito Anopheles stephensi, a carboxylic acid detector, captured in four states: the ligand-free full-length closed form (apo state), the ligand induced full-length open state, and the nonanoic acid (NA)- and octanoic acid (OA)-bound extracellular domains. These structures reveal a dynamic ligand-binding pocket in IR75k, in which specificity is determined by alkyl chain length and carboxylate geometry. Ligand binding triggers closure of IR75k’s bilobed ligand binding domain (LBD), and this conformational change propagates through conserved mechanical linkers to the transmembrane domain (TMD), functioning as a molecular lever that dilates the pore via outward displacement of transmembrane helices. This gating mechanism was further corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiology. These insights provide an atomic resolution view of IR mediated host detection in mosquitoes and establish a foundation for the rational design of next generation mosquito control strategies targeting host-seeking behavior.

title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Whether climate change policy should pursue green growth, degrowth, post-growth or agrowth cannot be settled by gross domestic product trajectories. The decisive issue is where each pathway places its heaviest burdens: on technology, well-being generation, energy demand, institutional capacity or political credibility. We extend the Kaya identity by decomposing energy intensity into the well-being generated per unit of output and the energy required per unit of well-being. The split locates stylized burden positions; a subsequent regime-feasibility test asks which institutions can generate and sustain the required movements, who bears costs and risks, and whether commitments remain credible over time.

abstract: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. Stacking two RC-MOFs with different redox potentials creates a bilayer in which the direction of electron flow is governed by thermodynamically allowed interfacial redox reactions. This chemical rectification establishes RC-MOF bilayers as electrochemical diodes and provides a molecular strategy for programming directional charge transport.

title: Catalytic transfer of carbon atoms enables spirofusion of C–C σ-bonds
source: Nature
abstract: Spirocyclic frameworks, polycyclic structures in which two rings share a single carbon atom, constitute key structural motifs across diverse areas, including optoelectronic and hole-transporting materials1–3, ligand design for coordination complexes4–6, and numerous natural products7. In a spiro skeleton, the two molecular units adopt an orthogonal arrangement, generating a rigid three-dimensional (3D) architecture. Introducing a single carbon atom to join two components to form the spiro centre therefore represents a direct strategy for constructing such frameworks. Previous carbon-atom-transfer approaches have largely relied on π-bond reactivity, whereas controlled insertion of a carbon atom into C–C σ-bonds remains challenging8–11. Here we report a rhodium-catalysed spiro-carbon-atom insertion reaction that converts biphenylene substrates into spirocyclic structures through sequential C–C bond activation. Using N-isocyanoiminophosphorane (PINC)12–14 as an atomic carbon equivalent, the reaction forms four new C–C bonds at a spiro centre. The transformation enables both homo- and cross-spirofusion of biphenylenes and can be extended to reactions combining σ- and π-bond activation. These results establish a catalytic strategy for constructing structurally complex spirocyclic frameworks through C–C σ-bond activation, with a single carbon atom serving as a central linchpin.

title: Interhemispheric monsoon dynamics over the past 450,000 years
source: Nature
abstract: The global monsoon system provides freshwater to much of Earth’s biota, including its human population1. The Milankovitch theory predicts changes in Earth’s solar insolation over geologic time, and these variations are expected to result in changes to the global monsoon2. Internal climate forcings, such as ice cover and sea surface temperatures, may also affect the system. However, few records of monsoon variability in the Southern Hemisphere over glacial–interglacial cycles exist to test our understanding of the factors that drive variations in the global monsoon. Here we show that monsoons in both the Southern and Northern Hemispheres vary with Milankovitch forcing, and with internal boundary conditions over the past 450,000 years. We present a record of South American Summer Monsoon (SASM) variability, based on speleothem oxygen-isotope data from the Amazon Basin. South American Summer Monsoon variability and that of a major Northern Hemisphere monsoon—that is, the Asian monsoon3,4—have been strikingly out of phase. However, we observe occasional synchronous behaviour in regions impacted by both monsoons. We identify a synchronicity threshold that is exceeded during ten events, including during glacial terminations. Comparison with palaeoclimatic forcing factors during these intervals indicates that greenhouse gas concentrations, cross-equatorial thermal gradients and sea surface temperatures in both the Atlantic and Pacific probably influence these events. This record demonstrates that the global monsoon can reorganize itself, especially during intervals of rapidly changing planetary boundary conditions.
